Build polygons from line segments

Source: R/spatial.R
tda_polygons.Rd

sdcpol takes a set of line segments, finds where they meet and assembles the polygons they enclose. It works on a plain table of segments rather than on a tda_spatial structure, and with option = 3 it writes a spatial data file the rest of the family can read.

Usage

tda_polygons(segments, option = 3, dir = tempfile("tda"), ...)

Arguments

segments

a data frame of four columns: the two ends of each segment, as x1, y1, x2, y2.

option

1 prints the node list of the graph the segments form, 2 its edge list, 3 constructs the polygons.

dir

working directory for the run.

...

further options for sdcpol; tol is the tolerance for treating two points as the same, default 1e-4.

Value

For option = 3 a tda_spatial structure; otherwise the run, with the table in $table.

See also

Other spatial analysis: plot.tda_spatial(), tda_map(), tda_read_dbf(), tda_read_shapefile(), tda_read_spatial, tda_sd(), tda_sd_analyses, tda_sd_ps3(), tda_spatial()

Examples

sq <- data.frame(x1 = c(0, 1, 1, 0), y1 = c(0, 0, 1, 1),
                 x2 = c(1, 1, 0, 0), y2 = c(0, 1, 1, 0))
tda_polygons(sq)
#> TDA spatial data (poly.sd)
#>   (no summary in the reader's output; see $run$output)
